title: Young nurse sparks fierce debate after revealing how she bought three homes by the age 25
text:
A young nurse who already has three properties at the age of 25 has responded to critics who criticized her success in the real estate market.
Keeley Starling caused a heated debate after uploading a Tiktok Video detailing how she and her husband Matt acquired her real estate empire in a relatively short space of time.
While many Australians were impressed with the success of the property of the Perth couple and eager to learn more, others criticized them on multiple purchases.
“Houses of hoarding should not be held during a housing crisis,” wrote a spectator.
Another aggregate: “Never lose your work, you will fuck.”
A third wrote: ‘Debt, debt, debt’.
But Mrs. Starling told Daily Mail Australia that she had “seen all the unpleasant comments and that it does not affect me as I have heard everything before.”
“I think many of the comments come from jealousy or people who may not understand what we are doing and what we will achieve from it,” he said.
Perth Woman Keeley Starling divided the Australians after sharing a Tiktok video that details how she and her husband Matt became a success in the real estate market
The couple has two properties in Perth, while the other is in Albany in the great southern region of WA.
Mrs. Starling attributes the success of her property to hard work.
She juggled with two work eight shifts for fifteen days as a nurse ‘and every two days I work in real estate’.
In addition to that, “after my nursing shifts, I always respond to emails or making calls,” he said.
His colleagues, unlike some online commentators, have been very supportive.
“I have had nothing more than praise of my nursing colleagues that has been a blessing,” Starling said.
Matt, who is a cartoonist, bought his first house four years ago, but as Keeley explained, “although he bought it before we were together, it is my house, it is his house.”
“All our finances are joint now and now I pay the mortgage (with it) and everything to do with the house.”
Keeley Starling (right) and her husband Matt (left) have found great success in the real estate market in Western Australia. The couple is shown in one of their three properties.
Mrs. Starling bought her first house with Matt last May.
“He had saved the money before we met and had all the finances ready,” he said.
“Although Matt did not pay for the deposit, we paid the mortgage together, so that is his second home.”
They just bought a third house, which will move next month.
Buying that house was quite simple for the couple, using the assets of one of their other properties to pay the deposit and rates.
“My advice for people trying to enter the real estate market is to think outside the box,” Starling said.
‘Look for properties in regional cities where prices are not as high as the city. I own a property in Albany, where the price was half of what I would pay in the city, but the rental performance is the same.
“Then, once that property has increased in value, it can extract the heritage to buy another.”
Mrs. Starling also had useful advice for any new person in the real estate market, but does not know how to set foot on the door.
“If you are thinking of entering the real estate market and is a bit nervous, do not think you have to save for rates and deposit for all houses,” he said.
Mrs. Starling works eight shifts for fifteen days as a nurse ‘and every two days I work in real estate’. She is photographed with her nurse’s uniform
‘You can get the capital to pay the later houses. (You should only make sure you have enough borrowing power and that you can serve the debt. ‘
She said “honestly he never thought he would be in this position in my life, especially at 25 of the houses.”
The couple has learned a lot about the real estate market to buy properties and rent them.
“There are still things that Matt and I are learning every day,” he said.
“There are things that we must do, such as reducing our monthly to biweekly payments for the two investments and then weekly (for) the main (home) because there are no tax benefits.”
He added that these are ‘things that are not taught at school.
“Honestly, we learned as we advanced and fortunately we are in this position where we have three houses together at age 25.
Mrs. Starling said the couple hopes to add their real estate empire in the future.
“But for now we want to focus on our current properties,” he said.
